verdicts.claim: A single published pre-write SHA-256, auto-verified on completion, cannot match bytes that the same delivery step rewrites per buyer.
verdicts.quoteCheck: All five 14.03.01 quotes verbatim at :73, :82, :89, :114, :184. 14.03.05:32 and :39 verbatim. 14.04.01:275 (D-06) and :293 (Q-07) verbatim. digital-goods-marketplace-cx.md:35 (CX-24) verbatim including 'two writers on one artifact'.
verdicts.reason: The watermark half of the contradiction survives and is genuinely silent. 14.03.05:32 'Marking makes each delivered artifact unique' and 14.03-delivery-versioning-library-cx.md:13 (CX-04) 'The watermark is stamped **during** delivery — it is per-buyer, so it cannot be pre-baked into a shared artifact' are irreconcilable with 14.03.01:89 'On completion, SHA-256 is verified automatically against the published checksum' plus :114 (E-19) quarantining the build on a second mismatch. The spec demonstrably reasons about watermarking's byte-level effect on verification twice — 14.03.01:105 (E-10) 'a per-buyer random mark shifts byte offsets… the file is garbage that fails verification', :123 (E-28) 'a new seed, so the partial is unusable' — and never once reconciles the delivered bytes with the *published artifact* hash. No decision, edge case, or open question in either file names the checksum consequence. DOWNGRADED from blocking on three grounds. (a) The MUST x MUST leg fails: 14.04.01:275 (D-06) embeds buyer-invariant tempo/key metadata, so an implementer converges on hashing the canonical delivered form and 14.03.01 (MUST, moscow-ledger.md:136) ships coherently — the MUST-band implementer is not blocked. (b) The residual is confined to 14.03.05, COULD-band (moscow-ledger.md:607) and vendor-opt-in per 14.03.05:37, with 14.03.05:97 (Q-03) still open on whether it is enabled at all. (c) D-09's hand-verification limb does not in fact collide: 14.03.05:21 scopes the Operator to 'None — Studios buy software (no audio payload to mark)' and 14.03.05:64 limits marking to audio, so the air-gapped copyable-hash workflow at 14.03.01:184 never meets a marked artifact. Partial tracking exists at 14.04.01:293 (Q-07, Owner Agent, target /create-prd-architecture) — 'which feature owns writing bytes at delivery?' — but it names caching and architecture as the consequence and is silent on integrity, so the checksum interaction is not covered by an existing question.

verdicts.claim: Decline/Empty states promise a 14-day cancel-for-full-refund while the same file forbids naming any cancellation right to non-EU/UK buyers, leaving the launch (US) path undetermined.
verdicts.reason: Refuted on two independent grounds. (1) No contradiction: 14.09.01:162 states the gate is 'Locale-selected wording', and :216 (D-08) locks 'the gate does **not** branch on territory; it fires for every buyer, and only the **wording** varies by locale.' E-01's quoted sentence is therefore the EU/UK instance of a locale-selected string, and E-20's neutral sentence is the non-EU instance of the same slot — the file states the branching rule explicitly rather than contradicting itself. Two implementers converge on one gate with a locale-keyed string table. (2) The residual product question is a tracked deferral that names this exact gap. 14.09.01:229 (Q-01) reads '`[OWNER]` … what is the refund policy above the statutory floor … **Sharpened by Q-04's resolution: with a US-first launch there is no statutory floor to sit above, so the policy is not a top-up — it is the entire consumer position.**' with Owner 'User' and Deferred To '/create-prd'. The auditor cites this line as proof of a gap; it is the documented mechanism for it, carrying both an owner and a target, and it was re-sharpened *because* of the Q-04 launch-market resolution the finding relies on. The structural half is also already settled independent of policy: 14.09.01:126 (E-02) 'No performance, so no waiver was ever needed' and 14.09.02:279 (D-06) 'A pre-delivery refund is a **cancellation**, not an adjudication' make the undelivered-order exit territory-neutral; only its window length awaits Q-01.

verdicts.claim: Five cells defer to a completed stage; four are Edge Case outcome cells leaving named failure modes with no behaviour and no owner.
verdicts.reason: Refuted on all four legs. (a) Depth policy: 14.02.02/14.02.04 are COULD (moscow-ledger.md:604, :605) and 14.02.03 is WONT (:750) — ideation-index.md:67 places all 254 Could/Won't features 'correctly out of Step 5 scope', so the marker records an allocation, not a lapse. (b) The CX cell at :109 sits in CX-05, labelled 'Medium confidence' at :104 with ':111 Synthesis questions: Deferred — Medium confidence; contingent on reseller integration being obtainable at all (14.02.03 Q-01)' — the documented confidence gate of D-25. (c) The fingerprint cell has a counterpart question in its own file: 14.02.02:91 '| Q-02 | How tolerant is the machine fingerprint to hardware change? Strict punishes legitimate upgrades; loose makes seats decorative. | Agent | `/create-prd-architecture` |' — owner and target present, same words as the cell. (d) The finding's strongest sub-claim — that the chargeback-fraud cell 'has no counterpart question anywhere in the unit' and an implementer must invent whether a card-theft victim is blacklisted — is refuted by the same file's locked decisions: 14.02.04:87 (D-01) 'Blacklisting is platform-adjudicated; vendors request, they do not execute' and :88 (D-02) 'Every enforcement action carries a reason, a notification, and an appeal route… Due process is also what makes a false positive survivable.' The behaviour for a false-positive victim is defined — adjudicated, notified, appealable — and 14.02.04:95 (Q-01) tracks the adjudication model itself to /create-prd.

verdicts.claim: An Edge Case cell describes a permanently-broken buyer state with no defined remedy, and no tracked question covers it.
verdicts.reason: The remedy the finding says must be invented — 'a refund, a substitute, or only a disclosure' — is specified across two files. Disclosure: 14.04.03:93 (D-02) 'Total completion cost (template + missing dependencies) is shown before the buy button' and :53 'this must be visible before purchase' → 'You're missing 4 of 11 dependencies — £340 to complete' *above* the buy button'; reinforced at 14.04-cx.md:96 'Template purchase does **not** grant its dependencies. Must be stated before purchase, loudly.' Refund: 14.09.02 owns the conformity path and adjudicates this exact shape at :181 'Preset bank references wavetables it does not ship… The product is unusable as delivered. `vendor-nonconformity` where the bundling field was declared and wrong; where the field does not exist yet… platform absorbs', with :63 grounding it in 'Conformity (not as described / not fit for purpose)' and :116 listing 'not as described' as a reason code. Materiality is also capped: 14.04.03 is COULD (moscow-ledger.md:608), out of Step 5 scope per ideation-index.md:67. The two CX cells are the Medium-confidence gate (:105 'Medium confidence', :111 'Deferred — Medium confidence') and question five of five in a high-confidence pair. The finding's F-01 restatement is scored under F-01.

verdicts.claim: The lease-vs-exclusive commit race has no defined outcome; the domain CX answers only the opposite ordering.
verdicts.reason: The mechanism, not just one ordering, is specified — and it is symmetric. digital-goods-marketplace-cx.md:359 resolves the lease/exclusive race 'at the same hard-lock as CX-15', and 14.05.02:39 'the transaction locks the listing (CX-01 — the race is the danger)' with :49 'Requires a hard lock, not read-then-write' and the loser's payment 'must never capture'. Under a hard lock the ordering is decided by whichever commits first in either direction, and 14.05.02:64 already gives the loser's terminal state generically: '| Error | Lost the race, or transfer failed | "Sold moments ago" / explicit failure — never an ambiguous state on a copyright |'. Two implementers building to a hard lock converge; neither can produce the finding's feared outcome (an exclusive silently encumbered by a lease that committed inside the lock). Materiality is capped — 14.05.02 is COULD (moscow-ledger.md:609), out of Step 5 scope (ideation-index.md:67) — and the unwind question that would remain is tracked at 14.05.02:99 (Q-04, Owner User, /create-prd). The role-scoping cell at 14.05-cx.md:110 is the Medium-confidence gate (:106 'Medium confidence', :112 'Deferred — Medium confidence, and contingent on index Q-01').

verdicts.claim: Two Edge Case cells (settlement against an un-deactivatable seat, dead-hardware return) carry no defined behaviour and no owner.
verdicts.reason: Both cells have counterpart questions in their own files, with owners and targets. 14.06.02:105 '| Q-02 | Who bears the loss when a transfer fails *after* the seller's licence was stripped but before the buyer's was written? Rollback should prevent it; if it can't, someone must. | Agent | `/create-prd-architecture` |' is the loss-allocation question the escrow cell raises, and 14.06.02:106 (Q-03, [OWNER]) still asks 'is the escrow worth building at all'. 14.06.03:99 '| Q-03 | If the hardware is returned after the licence transferred and the buyer has activated it on a machine that never comes back online, who eats the loss? | User | `/create-prd` |' is the dead-hardware cell restated as a tracked question one screen below the cell itself. The physics is also stated openly at digital-goods-marketplace-cx.md:231 'It inherits the same physics: under fail-open (14.02.02 D-01), a seller's offline machine keeps running after they sold the licence.' Lowest materiality in the domain: 14.06.02 is WONT (moscow-ledger.md:751) and 14.06.03 COULD (:612) — both out of Step 5 scope per ideation-index.md:67. The role-scoping cell at 14.06-cx.md:73 is the Medium-confidence gate.

verdicts.claim: Q-12 is marked RESOLVED while carrying a corrective action against another document with no owner and no deferral target.
verdicts.quoteCheck: The registration gap is real — ideation-cx.md:25 Serves list reads '03,04,05,06,13,16,17,20,24' with 14 absent. But 'no owner and no deferral target' is contradicted by the row the finding itself quotes. digital-goods-marketplace-index.md:131 gives the table header '| # | Question | Owner | Deferred To |', and the tail of :144 reads '…the participant list needs 14 added. | Agent | ✅ `ideation-cx.md` (Reviews, Ratings & Portable Reputation) + `digital-goods-marketplace-cx.md` escalation table |' — Owner is Agent and the Deferred To cell cites both registration sites.
verdicts.reason: Refuted on the misdescription and on materiality. The row carries an owner; the gap is not silent (it is written out verbatim in the row's own text, which is why the auditor could quote it); and the ownership answer is recorded on the domain side at digital-goods-marketplace-cx.md:549 '| **Reviews & Ratings** | 05, 13, 14, 16 |'. ideation-cx.md independently lists domain 14 as a reviews-adjacent participant across its pair table (e.g. :148 pair 88, :232 pair 172), so a downstream reader of ideation-cx.md alone is not led to conclude 14 is excluded from the store's reserved review surface. Nothing product-level is forced — the finding's own forcedInvention field concedes 'Nothing product-level'. This is a one-cell list-hygiene nit in a derived registry, not a vision-layer ambiguity.

verdicts.reason: An implementer can tell, because the same behaviour is stated three times in this file and once in a sibling, and the file's own edge-case table marks it closed. 14.03.05:48 '| Stamping fails mid-delivery | ~~Serve unmarked or fail the download?~~ **Resolved — this file's D-03**… | Nothing. Incident logged. |'; :63 '| Error | Stamping failed | Per the recommendation: download proceeds, incident logged; buyer sees nothing |'; and the MUST-band sibling builds on it as settled at 14.03.01:122 '| E-27 | Watermark stamping fails mid-delivery | Per 14.03.05 D-03: serve unmarked, log the incident, never block a paying buyer… **But** the grant must record that this artifact is unmarked'. The 'flagged for confirmation' phrase records residual product doubt about a posture already specified — which is exactly what the finding's own contrast case (14.02.02:83, 'Recorded as a recommendation, not a lock') also does — and it sits in a COULD-band, vendor-opt-in feature (moscow-ledger.md:607) whose existence is itself still open at 14.03.05:97 (Q-03).
